summary: Sync Jira project lifecycle to Slack + Confluence: auto-provision admin group, channel, space and enforce archival
description:
Issue summary: We need an automated workflow that ensures when a new Jira project is created under our internal org template it automatically provisions a scoped admin group, creates a Slack channel and Confluence space following naming and access policies, and when the Jira project is archived the channel/space are moved to an archival state (pinned read-only + retention notification) and the admin group is deprovisioned.

Impact: Manual provisioning is slowing team onboarding, causing permission drift, and producing orphaned channels/spaces that complicate audits. This automation reduces manual work, enforces naming conventions and retention policy, and closes gaps flagged during last quarter's compliance review.

Environment: Applies to internal Redwood Jira projects using the "team-pod" project template in prod. Slack workspaces: #redwood-core and #redwood-comm; Confluence root: /internal/projects. IAM managed in Okta; group lifecycle via our RBAC sync service.
acceptance_criteria: 1) When a Jira project is created using the team-pod template, the automation creates: a) a group (jira-<projectkey>-admins) in Okta, b) a Slack channel (#proj-<projectkey>-team) with topic and discovery tags, and c) a Confluence space with the standard project blueprint. 2) Permissions are applied: group added as admin to both Slack channel and Confluence space. 3) When Jira project is transitioned to Archived state, the automation marks the Slack channel read-only (channel posting disabled), adds an archival banner to the Confluence space, notifies listed owners, and schedules deletion/retention per policy. 4) All actions are logged to the Audit pipeline and an event is emitted to #internal-ops for visibility.
implementation_notes: Prefer using existing provisioning lambda (ops-provisioner) and extend with a lifecycle webhook from Jira Cloud to avoid polling.
Okta group creation should use the existing service-account and follow naming guardrails; work with identity to validate SCIM attributes.
Slack changes must use the workspace app token with admin scope; ensure rate-limit handling for bulk project onboarding.
Confluence space creation should use our project blueprint and add standardized page templates; attach space permissions to newly created Okta group.
Emit structured events to kafka topic 'project-lifecycle-events' for downstream auditing and metrics.
Add feature flag in the orchestration service to enable rollout to a pilot pod before full enablement.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated deletion/archival could remove data unexpectedly if project keys are reused. Mitigation: enforce a two-step archival (mark -> notify owners -> archive after 7 days) and require explicit confirmation for permanent deletion. Add guardrail that prevents automation from acting on projects older than 365 days without manual review.
notes_from_triage: Triage call 2026-03-11: Priority set to P2. Suggested pilot with three pods (model-eval, infra-intel, solutions) and feature flag gating. Identity and security should sign off on Okta SCIM attributes and audit log schema. Operations to estimate runbook updates and monitoring needs.
work_items: Create Jira webhook subscription for project create/update/archive events.
Extend ops-provisioner lambda with handlers for create/archive events.
Add Okta group provisioning logic and map to Slack/Confluence permissions.
Add audit event emission and update internal dashboards for provisioning success/failure.
Draft runbook for manual override and rollback.
Pilot enablement and collect metrics for 2 weeks before full rollout.
estimated_effort: 3 Sprints (design + prototype 1 sprint, pilot + monitoring 1 sprint, rollout + docs 1 sprint)
